sinkline.name: sinkline
sinkline.title: sinkline: taint analysis for Python web apps | Sami Ali
sinkline.desc: sinkline follows request data across functions and files to sinks. On OWASP BenchmarkPython it scores +0.52 on taint categories vs Bandit +0.07, and trails Bandit over all 14.
sinkline.fact: A static analyzer that follows request data across functions and files and reports it only when it reaches a dangerous sink without a sanitizer for that bug class. 138 tests; scored on OWASP BenchmarkPython v0.1.

failed_first.text: The stock SigmaHQ Setuid and Setgid rule matched 0 of 36 recorded events. A replacement rule matches the 2 chmod executions.
4 of the 7 Windows scenarios have no accepted recording yet and count as zero in the 68% weighted coverage.

On the independent OWASP BenchmarkPython suite, 0.4.1 scored +0.21 on the 10 taint categories, with 0 of 16 LDAP and 5 of 51 XPath cases reported. 0.5.0 scores +0.52, but the fixes were chosen from those failures, so it is not a held-out score.
Over all 14 categories Bandit leads (+0.36 against +0.27): sinkline has no check for weak hashes, weak random numbers, cookie flags or session contents.
The GitHub Action put its inputs into a shell line, a script-injection flaw in its own code. Fixed in 0.4.1.
Six defects survived 227 tests, including a non-constant-time key comparison. 0.1.1 adds tests that kill all six.
The image parser accepted ghcr.io/org/../evil, and ignoreUnfixed could let a KEV finding with no fix pass denyKev. Both are fixed in v0.1.0.
The harness treated any folded-header error in strict mode as the documented deviation, which would have hidden a real bug. The exception is now narrowed.

Earlier text called the score "in the spirit of" CISA BOD 26-04, and a measurements table reported properties of invented values. Both were corrected: it is a weighted score of its own design, and the table was removed.
